question: A 24-year-old professional athlete is advised to train in the mountains to enhance his performance. After 5 months of training at an altitude of 1.5 km (5,000 feet), he is able to increase his running pace while competing at sea-level venues. Which of the following changes would produce the same effect on the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve as this athlete's training did?
analysis: Training at high altitudes leads to physiological adaptations that shift the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve to the right, allowing for improved oxygen delivery to tissues. This is due to increased levels of 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate (2,3-BPG) in red blood cells, which enhances oxygen unloading at the tissues. Therefore, the option that would produce a similar effect on the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve is decreased 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate.
